head: 6b91dea8b89f7c0480a0373ebd7d94d03a575de0
summary: SL-080 set out to A/B de51999 against HEAD to see if the 860px default window height worsens T-005's move/resize stall on real D:\; two risk-spikes proved that literal comparison impossible (de51999 predates the FolderTree feature; 33 files differ beyond height), so the design substituted a same-build ABBA height test plus an EventPipe-traced stack-attribution tool, both built and validated live. Three build attempts and five code-review passes were spent almost entirely on discovering and fixing where in WPF's window lifecycle the test hook must apply height to avoid confounding the measurement with its own resize. The delivered answer: 860px shows no measurable height effect on the stall, and the real blocking frame is WPF's synchronous render path (DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush), reproduced live by validate; the companion GPU-vs-render-thread question is left unresolved because the Render batch's own verdict didn't hold up under re-measurement.

candidates.title: Design a fix for the WPF render-path SyncFlush stall at scan/rescan start
candidates.why: validate's live traced run put 93.6% of the matched busy stretch in DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush, and StallStacks named RENDER-PATH reliably — this is the actual root-cause narrowing the epic wanted; a fix slice is the natural next step now that the diagnostic tooling holds.

candidates.title: Re-run the Trace and Render batches under the current (pre-handle) height sizing with a full 8-pair schedule
candidates.why: validate found the shipped Render verdict (render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu) does not reproduce live (reads inconclusive, ratio 0.56); render-2 was run under superseded sizing and its 4-pair schedule could only detect a 5.41x difference.

candidates.title: Re-check the GC-suspension finding (≤1% of longest wait) at multi-GB / multi-million-file scan scale
candidates.why: the spike verdict is explicitly conditional on retained heaps up to ~110MB; the epic targets ~5M-file drives, where a blocking Gen2 collection could be a much larger share of the rescan stall.

candidates.title: Get a person's decision on what 'real D:\' means for this stall investigation
candidates.why: this exact question has been raised twice (SL-044's reflection and SL-080's own design) without a person answering it, and every measurement this slice produced depends on the synthetic-tree reading being the one the epic meant.

candidates.title: Trace the ~1.3s later-move stall separately from the ~340ms first-move stall
candidates.why: it appeared as the largest wait in 5-12 of 16 runs across this slice's batches, in both arms, but no traced run landed on it — the current findings only speak to the first-move stall.

candidates.title: Build the FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG in-process dispatcher/WM_* timestamping fallback
candidates.why: it exists only as a contract (from O-012); no Trace batch has yet hit CANNOT-READ or tracing-masks to require it, but it's owed the day EventPipe attribution hits its ceiling.

candidates.title: Decide whether an elevated ETW/WPR capture is authorized for one diagnostic session on this app
candidates.why: design's own open question 2 is still unresolved, but unelevated EventPipe has so far named the blocking frame successfully (RENDER-PATH), so this is only needed if that mechanism later fails.

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium/medium-risk with a single designer, sized by a person. That undercounted the build side badly: 3 build attempts and 5 code-review passes were needed, and almost all of that rework was one mechanical question — does FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT apply before or after the scan starts — that the design and critique both treated as already true (the component description says 'before the first scan starts') rather than verified against MainWindow.xaml.cs's actual OnLoaded→StartScan order. Meanwhile the risk the design and critique spent their attention on — whether unelevated EventPipe sampling could name a real frame on a WPF UI thread, the design's own highest-risk, unrun bet — held on the very first live traced run and needed no rework at all. The estimate was wrong in the direction of trusting an assumed-true mechanical detail and worrying about an assumed-risky novel one; it should have been the other way around.

learned.lesson: MainWindow.xaml.cs's OnLoaded handler calls StartScan before its first await, so a test hook that must act 'before the scan starts' has to run before the window even has a handle (a Dispatcher.Hooks watch installed pre-Main) — Loaded-class handlers and even SourceInitialized are both too late and both still leave a resize-of-an-already-rendered-window confound.
learned.evidence: 3 build attempts (Loaded handler → SourceInitialized → pre-handle BeforeMain dispatcher watch) before the height-850-2 control batch measured the two arms equal at load.

learned.lesson: FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT already existed from an earlier slice (TreeMode.Size); the actual risk in this slice was never the knob's existence (critique's m5 caught that) but its timing relative to scan start, which nobody checked against the code until code-review.
learned.evidence: code-review found the same timing defect twice, in attempt 1 (M1) and attempt 3 (M3), each time requiring a fresh build attempt to fix.

learned.lesson: design-slice's own open questions ('what does real D:\ mean', 'authorize elevated ETW?') were never answered by a person before the slice proceeded; design-slice halted once on them, then re-ran and passed with 'Accept SL-080 attempt 1' and no recorded person decision, carrying both questions forward unresolved through build and validate.
learned.evidence: design-slice #1 halted on the 2 questions; design-slice #2 passed without either being answered, and both are still listed open at the end of the slice.

learned.lesson: The GC-suspension spike (≤1% of longest wait) and the CPU/worker-load spike (stall persists 18/18 regardless) are settled facts for this app at T-005's ~110MB scale — future move-stall work shouldn't re-spike either, but the GC result specifically should be re-checked once a real multi-GB scan is in scope.
learned.evidence: spike constraint: 'Verified only for retained heaps up to ~110 MB... re-run this same spike against a much larger tree before assuming the same near-zero GC share holds there.'

learned.lesson: Unelevated EventPipe CPU sampling via dotnet-trace can name a concrete managed frame on this app's WPF UI thread (DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush, 93.6% of the matched stretch) — the design's single highest-risk, never-spiked bet held on the first live run, so future diagnostic slices on this UI thread can build directly on StallStacks.ps1 rather than re-verifying the mechanism.
learned.evidence: validate's live Trace batch: 'The scan's first move waited 337.4 ms... 93.6% of the stretch in DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush.'

learned.lesson: The Render plan's 2-block/4-pair schedule is under-powered for a GPU-vs-render-thread call; any Render verdict from fewer than 8 pairs (the Height plan's schedule) should be treated as provisional, not delivered.
learned.evidence: validate: 'render-2's 4 pairs could only have detected a 5.41x difference'; validate's own live Render batch under the same undersized schedule read inconclusive.

learned.lesson: A diagnostic/chase slice whose deliverable is 'trust this measurement tool's number' should be sized assuming the tool's own measurement mechanism needs a debugging cycle of its own, separate from the C#/PowerShell code quality it's reviewed for.
learned.evidence: build-slice ran 3 times and code-review ran 5 times, mostly re-litigating one measurement-timing question rather than finding new code defects.

missed.what: The design's own component description claims FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT is applied 'before the first scan starts', but critique never checked this against MainWindow.xaml.cs's actual OnLoaded→StartScan call order — a one-file read would have shown the claim was false as of when the design was written.
missed.caught_by: code-review (attempt 1, finding M1, and again in attempt 3, finding M3, after the first fix attempt still left it false)

missed.what: code-review's final pass (attempt 5) accepted the doc's delivered Render verdict (render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu) as a documented-but-not-required-to-fix note, even though it was measured under sizing that attempt 3's own findings had proven wrong; it did not require a re-run before letting the slice's findings ship as settled.
missed.caught_by: validate, whose live Render batch under current sizing read inconclusive (ratio 0.56), directly contradicting the shipped doc's conclusion

payload.reason: Validate reproduced the delivered Height and Trace verdicts live and found no blocker; the one thing it could not reproduce (the Render verdict) was already an explicitly flagged open item, not a silent gap, so the slice completes with that item carried forward rather than as an unresolved failure.

Three build attempts and five code-review passes were spent almost entirely on discovering and fixing where in WPF's window lifecycle the test hook must apply height to avoid confounding the measurement with its own resize. The delivered answer: 860px shows no measurable height effect on the stall, and the real blocking frame is WPF's synchronous render path (DUCE+Channel.SyncFlush), reproduced live by validate; the companion GPU-vs-render-thread question is left unresolved because the Render batch's own verdict didn't hold up under re-measurement.
unknowns: Is the render-path SyncFlush wait during scan/rescan start GPU-bound or render-thread/DWM-bound? The delivered verdict didn't reproduce live and needs a full 8-pair Render batch to settle.
Does the ~1.3s later-move stall (distinct from the ~340ms first-move stall this slice measured) share the same SyncFlush cause, or is it a different mechanism? No traced run has hit it yet.
Does GC share stay near-zero during a rescan of a real multi-GB, multi-million-file drive, or does it grow with retained-heap size the way the current ~110MB-verified spike can't show?
Does 'real D:\' in the epic's own language mean T-005's synthetic tree redirected onto D:\, or an actual scan of whatever data lives on D:\? Two design-slice cycles have now left this unanswered.
what_went_wrong: risk-spike ran twice: the first attempt spent a full run discovering de51999 has no FolderTree/T-005 before checking `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, a check that could have ruled it out before any run.

design-slice ran twice; the two open questions it raised (what 'real D:\' means, whether elevated ETW is authorized) were never answered by a person, and the slice proceeded anyway on the second pass.

build-slice ran 3 times solely over where in WPF's lifecycle the hook applies window height relative to scan start (Loaded handler → SourceInitialized → a pre-handle Dispatcher watch installed before Main); each earlier fix was disproven by its own control batch (a 10px height-850-vs-860 comparison still showing the whole gap).

code-review ran 5 times: 3 of those passes were spent on the same height-timing confound (M1 in attempt 1, M3 in attempt 3), and one was spent on a relative-path defect (R2-M2) that silently discarded every EventPipe trace the Trace plan produced.

The delivered Render verdict (render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu) was measured under sizing later proven wrong and was never re-run before being written into the findings doc; validate's live re-run reads inconclusive instead, contradicting the shipped conclusion.
